brief: Deutsche Bank raised its Meta price target to $820 from $750, now based on 25x FY27 EPS (previously 23x), driven by early Muse traction. Muse downloads have outpaced prior AI app launches (over 3mn US installs in its first 16 days, #1 Productivity app on iOS with 4.9 stars), which DB reads as strong product-market fit. Meta's free tier is generous (100mn tokens/week), so DB sees little near-term incentive for users to upgrade to paid Power ($20/mo) or Maximum ($100/mo) tiers; DB thinks Meta is building the user base first and will monetize later, possibly by narrowing free limits over time. DB sketches three monetization paths: subscription upsell, a transaction take-rate on partner commerce (partnerships include Walmart, Best Buy, Gap, Sephora, Instacart, Wayfair, PayPal, Stripe, Shopify, Expedia), and advertising within the Muse feed. DB estimates Muse could reach ~Mid-SD% of 2030 revenue (HSD in an upside case), though it flags this as early and uncertain. Provisioning runs $25-50/user in capex versus $3.50-6.50/month base hosting cost per user. Separately, DB maps agentic-commerce implications across its coverage: Booking likely follows Expedia into Muse, Airbnb and Chewy look relatively insulated, and Amazon may eventually need a negotiated integration.
